 : Order :

This writ petition is filed to declare the action of respondents in seeking to acquire the house bearing No.5-56/1 built in 240 Sq.Yards, situated at Gandhipuram, Anantharam Village, Mahabubabad Mandal and District, for the purpose of constructing a government office i.e. Anganwadi School,
without initiating proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act No.30 of 2013 and without paying compensation, as illegal and arbitrary and for consequential relief.

2. Heard Sri A.Prabhakar Rao, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Putta Krishna Reddy,
learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.2.

No representation on behalf of respondent Nos.3 to 6.
3.

While the matter stood thus, respondent Nos.2 and 4 visited petitioner's subject property and informed the petitioner to vacate the house constructed in the subject property (subject house) on the ground that the same is required for construction of Government building i.e.
Anganwadi School, without any right or authority.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the subject property does not belong to Government and that in fact it is a private patta land belonging to one Smt.Peduru Lakshmi.

He Gandamalla Yakamma vs The State Of Telangana on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102373753/
1 further submits that on 04.06.2020, the respondent Nos. 2 and 5, again visited the subject property and tried to demolish the subject, without issuing any notice and without following due process.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the same, present writ petition is filed.

5. This Court vide order dated 09.06.2020 directed the respondents not to demolish the subject house and also further ordered that the petitioner shall not make any further construction, without obtaining the statutory permission as may be required.

6. Learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.2 by referring to the counter would submit that the officials of respondent No.2 did not ask the petitioner to vacate the subject house; that in fact they only informed the petitioner that the construction in the subject property was made, unauthorisedly,
without obtaining any permission.

He further submits that there is no proposal to convert the subject house into Anganwadi School; and that the respondents would follow due process, in accordance with the Telangana Municipalities Act, 2019, against the unauthorized construction, if any made by the petitioner.

7. In the light of the aforesaid submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.2, the writ petition is disposed of with a direction to respondents not to interfere with the possession of the petitioner's house, except in accordance with law.

However, this will not preclude the respondents from taking any action against the unauthorized constructions, if any, made by the petitioner, by duly following the procedure as contemplated under the Telangana Municipalities Act, 2019.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petition, shall stand closed.

LAXMI NARAYANA ALISHETTY, J Date:
